sections.label: Bill amendments six themes
sections.summary: The Bill follows a review and covers six themes, starting with increased deterrence against scams through caning.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: We made major amendments in 2019 and 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: We have since completed another round of review, which has culminated in this Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The amendments in the Bill cover six themes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: First, increase deterrence against scams by introducing caning as a punishment, while re-calibrating its use in other offences.

sections.label: Caning for scammers and mules
sections.summary: Amendments introduce caning for scammers and scam mules, with about 190,000 cases and $3.7 billion lost from 2020 to mid-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The first category of amendments will enhance deterrence against scams by introducing caning for scammers and scam mules, while re-calibrating its use in other offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Between 2020 and the first half of 2025, there were about 190,000 cases reported, with losses amounting to about $3.7 billion.

sections.label: Caning for remote communication scams
sections.summary: Clause 64 amends section 420 of the Penal Code so scam offenders face at least six strokes of the cane.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Clause 64 of the Bill amends section 420 of the Penal Code so that offenders who commit scams, defined as cheating mainly by means of remote communication, will be punished with at least six strokes of the cane.

sections.label: Caning for scam syndicate members
sections.summary: Clauses 37 and 38 create Organised Crime Act offences with mandatory caning of at least six strokes for scam syndicate members and recruiters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Clauses 37 and 38 of the Bill introduce new offences in the Organised Crime Act so that members of and recruiters for scam syndicates will be subject to mandatory caning of at least six strokes, if they knew that the organised criminal group was a scam syndicate.

sections.label: Scam cases and losses 2025
sections.summary: In the first half of 2025, there were almost 20,000 cases and almost half a billion dollars lost.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In the first half of 2025, there were almost 20,000 cases and almost half a billion dollars lost.

sections.label: Discretionary caning for vandalism
sections.summary: Clauses 72 to 74 amend the Vandalism Act to replace mandatory caning with discretionary caning for vandalism of public and designated private property.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Clauses 72 to 74 of the Bill amend the Vandalism Act so that mandatory caning is replaced with discretionary caning for vandalism of public property and designated private property.

sections.label: Enhanced penalties for obscene materials
sections.summary: Clause 42 introduces enhanced penalties under section 292(1) of the Penal Code for circulating obscene materials electronically to 10 or more persons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Clause 42 of the Bill therefore introduces enhanced penalties for offences under section 292(1) of the Penal Code where obscene materials are circulated by electronic means to 10 or more persons.

sections.label: Penalty for obscene material depicting minors
sections.summary: If obscene material depicts a minor below 18, penalty is mandatory imprisonment of up to four years, doubling the current two-year maximum.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: If the obscene material depicts a minor below the age of 18, the penalty will be mandatory imprisonment of up to four years, a doubling of the current maximum of two years' imprisonment.

sections.label: Penalties for circulating obscene material
sections.summary: The offence carries a fine and mandatory imprisonment of up to five years, or seven years if the material depicts a minor below 18.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Given the seriousness of such conduct, the offence is punishable with a fine and mandatory imprisonment of up to five years, or seven years if the obscene material circulated depicts a minor below the age of 18.

sections.label: Enhanced penalties for obscene materials depicting minors
sections.summary: Clause 42 extends enhanced penalties for obscene materials under section 292 to materials depicting minors below 18, up from 16.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: First, clause 42 of the Bill extends enhanced penalties for offences relating to obscene materials under section 292 of the Penal Code to obscene materials depicting minors below the age of 18, up from the current threshold of 16.

sections.label: Penalties for fatal abuse of vulnerable persons
sections.summary: Clauses 45 and 46 increase penalties for fatal abuse of vulnerable persons under sections 304B and 304C to life imprisonment or up to 30 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Third, clauses 45 and 46 of the Bill will increase the penalties for fatal abuse of vulnerable persons under sections 304B and 304C of the Penal Code to life imprisonment, or up to 30 years' imprisonment if life imprisonment is not imposed.

sections.label: Removal of requirement by clause 68
sections.summary: Clause 68 of the Bill removes this requirement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Clause 68 of the Bill removes this requirement.

sections.label: Doxxing public servant offence
sections.summary: Clause 25 creates an offence criminalising doxxing of a public servant accompanied by a known or believed falsehood.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Second, clause 25 of the Bill introduces a new offence in the Miscellaneous Offences Act to criminalise the doxxing of a public servant, when accompanied by a falsehood about the public servant that the offender knows or has reason to believe is false.

sections.label: Youth Court jurisdiction age
sections.summary: In 2019 the Government amended the Children and Young Persons Act to expand Youth Court jurisdiction to offenders below 18, up from 16.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In 2019, the Government moved the amendments to the Children and Young Persons Act (CYPA) to expand the jurisdiction of the Youth Court to all offenders below the age of 18, up from the previous age of 16.

sections.label: Reformative training imprisonment caning
sections.summary: It ensures reformative training, imprisonment and caning are available in such cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In particular, it ensures that reformative training, imprisonment and caning are available in such cases.

sections.label: Waiting period for goods dealers
sections.summary: Amendments increase the waiting period from three to five days, applying only to the worker or dealer who first receives goods from a customer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The amendments to the Miscellaneous Offences Act will increase the waiting period before such workers or dealers can work on or deal with goods sold to them, from three days to five.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: At the same time, we are reducing the scope of the requirement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: This waiting period will only apply to the worker or dealer who first receives goods from a customer; and not the worker or dealer who receives the goods from another dealer.

sections.label: Mandatory imprisonment obscene materials
sections.summary: The amendments introduce mandatory imprisonment of up to five years, with a higher maximum if obscene materials depict minors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: The current amendments introduce mandatory imprisonment of up to five years, with a higher maximum if the obscene materials circulated depict minors.

sections.label: Mandatory caning for scammers
sections.summary: The amendments introduce mandatory caning for scammers of minimum six strokes, while the law provides maximum imprisonment of only 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: The amendments before us today introduce mandatory caning for scammers, minimum six strokes, which I fully support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: But the law also provides for maximum imprisonment of only 10 years for scammers.

sections.label: Stiffer penalties for scam syndicates
sections.summary: Speaker suggests minimum six strokes and five years, maximum 15 strokes and 20 years for scam syndicate members and recruiters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: But the law also provides for maximum imprisonment of only five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: So, for scam syndicate members and recruiters, I would like to suggest much stiffer penalties, again: a minimum of six strokes and five years; and the maximum of 15 strokes and 20 years, to bring these penalties in line with those for traffickers of Class A drugs in most instances.

sections.label: Proportionate penalties for scam mules
sections.summary: Speaker suggests mules get maximum six strokes and five years, with minimum two years, instead of 12 strokes and 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: I will peg them closer to traffickers of Class C drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: And therefore, in my view, the penalties introduced by the amendments before us today for scam mules appear somewhat disproportionately harsh, compared to the penalties being introduced for scammers and scam syndicate members and recruiters higher up the scam crime chain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: For example, if the Bill today is passed, a mule who provides accounts or arrangements to launder scam proceeds, in particular, will face discretionary caning of up to 12 strokes and also maximum imprisonment of 10 years, compared to, as I said before, maximum imprisonment of five years for being a scam syndicate member or recruiter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: So, I suggest more proportionate penalties for all types of scam mules: discretionary caning with a maximum of six strokes instead of 12 and maximum imprisonment of five years but, also, I would like to suggest a minimum of two years, to bring these penalties more in line with those for trafficking Class C drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: I believe these suggested penalties, especially the minimum imprisonment of two years, will sufficiently deter specific offenders and would-be offenders from offending in future.

sections.label: Organised Crime Act scam offences
sections.summary: The Act is amended to create offences of being a member or recruiter of organised scam groups, with fines, jail and caning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, the Organised Crime Act is being amended to create two new offences; of being a member of a locally linked organised scam group and being a recruiter for organised scam groups, whether locally linked or not.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Besides setting high fines and jail time of up to five years, mandatory caning of at least six strokes is to be imposed.

sections.label: Cambodia scam ring arrests
sections.summary: Media covered a Cambodia scam ring; Cambodian and Singapore police arrested 15 suspects, including 12 Singaporeans, charged here.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the past week, there was extensive media coverage on a scam ring in Cambodia, apparently led by a Singaporean and staffed by scores of compatriots.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was reported that the Cambodian police conducted a joint operation with Singapore Police on 9 September, after which 15 suspects, including 12 Singaporeans, were arrested and charged here.

sections.label: Bill changes caning provisions
sections.summary: The Bill removes caning entirely for certain offences and makes it optional instead of mandatory for others.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes the total removal of caning as a punishment for certain offences and for others, making caning optional instead of mandatory.

sections.label: Vandalism caning made optional
sections.summary: The Bill removes mandatory caning of three to eight strokes for all vandalism offences, public and private property.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill removes the rigidity of the current Act, where mandatory caning of between three to eight strokes must be imposed on vandalism of both public and private property, except in limited circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill instead proposes that mandatory caning be removed for all vandalism offences.

sections.label: Doxxing public servants offence
sections.summary: Clause 25 creates an offence of publishing identity information and false statements about public servants connected to their duties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 25 creates a new offence in the Miscellaneous Offences Act of doxxing of public servants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the proposed section 14E, it will be an offence for anyone to publish identity information and false statements about public servants, if connected to the discharge of their duties.

sections.label: Enhanced obscene objects penalties
sections.summary: The Bill proposes enhanced penalties for sale, distribution or large-scale electronic circulation of obscene objects, especially those depicting minors, raising the age threshold from 16 to 18.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes enhanced penalties for the sale, distribution or large-scale electronic circulation of obscene objects, particularly those depicting minors, with the age threshold also being raised from 16 to 18.

sections.label: Synthetic intimate images risks
sections.summary: The amendments seek to deal with risks of synthetic, AI-generated intimate images, including deepfakes and computer-generated child abuse materials.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The amendments also seek to deal with the risks of synthetic, AI-generated intimate images, including "deepfakes" and computer-generated child abuse materials under our criminal laws.

sections.label: Disclosure with falsehood offence
sections.summary: A new offence targets disclosing a public servant's identity with a falsehood intended to prevent or deter the discharge of their duties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: A new offence targets the disclosure of a public servant's identity accompanied by a falsehood, when intended to prevent or deter the discharge of their duties.

sections.label: Caning for scammers and mules
sections.summary: Mandatory caning for scammers and syndicate members and discretionary caning for mules will signal that Singapore will not tolerate those who prey on its people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Mandatory caning for scammers and syndicate members, and discretionary caning for so-called "mules" will send an unequivocal signal: Singapore will not tolerate those who prey on our people, be it from behind a keyboard or through sophisticated networks.

sections.label: Support for obscene images provisions
sections.summary: The speaker supports provisions to penalise production of computer-generated obscene images, strengthen penalties for obscene objects involving minors under 18, and expand sexual grooming offences to meetings outside Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, I support the provisions to explicitly penalise the production of computer-generated obscene images to strengthen penalties for obscene objects involving minors below the age of 18 and to expand the scope of sexual grooming offences to cover meetings outside of Singapore.

sections.label: Protection of public servants and vulnerable victims
sections.summary: The Bill assures public servants they can discharge duties safely and increases prison terms for fatal abuse of vulnerable victims like children and domestic workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill provides our public servants with the necessary assurance that they can safely and securely discharge their duties without the threat of public harassment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I support how the Bill increases prison terms for causing or allowing the fatal abuse of vulnerable victims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This includes children and domestic workers who are often defenceless and cannot fight back.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We are sending the right message by increasing the sentences, which can go up to 30 years or life imprisonment to ensure that the vulnerable are protected.

sections.label: Sanctions against scam criminal organisations
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government could impose sanctions, financial sanctions or asset confiscation on criminal organisations scamming Singaporeans, possibly funding a victim restitution fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On another note, I want to ask whether there is the possibility of the Government imposing sanctions against criminal organisations involved in scamming Singaporeans, similar to what has been done in other jurisdictions, like the United States (US).

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can financial sanctions or asset confiscation be viable options to pursue with a view of, perhaps, using the recovered funds to finance a scam victim restitution fund of sorts?

sections.label: Reservations about caning for scam offences
sections.summary: The speaker questions whether caning's marginal deterrent value exceeds that of longer prison sentences for scam-related offences, calling this a constructive intervention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is worth reiterating that this is not a question of whether scammers should be harshly punished; of course, they should be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, the pertinent question is whether the marginal deterrent value of a longer prison sentence matches or even exceeds the marginal deterrent value of imposing caning as a penalty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope my reservations about caning for scam-related offences are also seen in the right way – that is, as a constructive intervention to ask whether caning is truly the most effective means of protecting Singaporeans from the scourge of scams.

sections.label: Six key areas of Bill updates
sections.summary: The Bill updates six key areas: deterrence against scams and tech-enabled crimes, penalties for abuse of vulnerable victims, sexual offence laws including AI-generated intimate images, a new offence for false statements or doxxing public officers, consistency in scanning and sentencing, and youth offender procedures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This Bill makes updates in six key areas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It strengthens deterrence against scams and tech-enabled crimes, increasing penalties for abuse of vulnerable victims and update laws on sexual offences, including AI-generated intimate images.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It introduces a new offence for spreading false statements or doxxing public officers, align scanning and sentencing provisions for greater consistency and refines procedures for youth offenders to balance rehabilitation and accountability.

sections.label: Caning for scam syndicates and enablers
sections.summary: The Bill introduces caning as an additional penalty for scam syndicates and their enablers, including those who provide SIM cards or launder criminal proceeds.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The emotional trauma often outlasts the financial loss.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This Bill introduces caning as an additional penalty for scam syndicates and their enablers: those who knowingly Singpass credentials provide SIM cards or launder criminal proceeds.

sections.label: New offence for doxxing public officers
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a new offence for publishing an officer's identity with a falsehood to deter or punish them for duties, and amends POHA to remove the need to prove harassment or distress.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: These incidents illustrate how misinformation can quickly erode trust and endanger the morale of those who serve the public.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This Bill rightly introduces a new offence under the Miscellaneous Offences, Public Order and Nuisance Act for publishing an officer's identity, together with a falsehood, when done to deter or punish them for carrying out their duties.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It also amends POHA to remove the need to prove that the officer suffered harassment or distress.

sections.label: POFMA and doxxing falsehood offence
sections.summary: Asks when agencies will use POFMA to correct misinformation and when the new doxxing with falsehood offence will protect individual officers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: When will agencies invoke POFMA to correct misinformation and when will they use the new doxxing with falsehood offence to protect individual officers?

sections.label: Protection for outsourced essential workers
sections.summary: Asks whether protection extends to outsourced essential workers such as cleaners, healthcare assistants or transport enforcement officers who perform public duties but are not statutory officers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Will protection also extend to outsourced essential workers, such as cleaners, healthcare assistants, or transport enforcement officers, who perform public duties, but are not statutory officers.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: States that notwithstanding the clarifications sought, the speaker supports this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the clarifications I sought, I support this Bill.

sections.label: Scam losses in Singapore
sections.summary: States that since 2019 Singaporeans lost over S$3 billion to scams, with over S$1.1 billion lost in 2024 and government-official impersonation scams nearly reaching 1,800 in the first half of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Since 2019, Singaporeans have lost over S$3 billion to scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In 2024 alone, losses were over S$1.1 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In the first half of this year, government-official impersonation scams almost reach 1,800, nearly triple year-on-year.

sections.label: Graduated charging for young offenders
sections.summary: Urges the Government, led by the Ministry of Law, to adopt a graduated, age-sensitive charging approach for those aged 14 to 18 to avoid the cliff effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: To avoid the cliff effect, where the full weight of adult liability falls on, say, a 14-year-old, I urge the Government, led by the Ministry of Law, to adopt a graduated, age-sensitive charging approach for those from 14 to18, which means calibrating charging positions and legal submissions based on age, maturity and context, and reserving adult-style positions for truly serious crimes.

sections.label: Caning for scam-related offences
sections.summary: States that for scam-related offences such as misuse of SIM cards or disclosing access credentials like Singpass accounts, the Bill allows up to 12 strokes of the cane under discretionary caning.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For scam-related offences such as offenders who facilitate scams such as the misuse of SIM cards, disclosing access credentials such as Singpass account, this Bill allows for up to 12 strokes of the cane under discretionary caning.

sections.label: Cambodian syndicate scam suspects named
sections.summary: Police named 27 Singaporeans and seven Malaysians suspected of running a Cambodian-based scam ring behind at least 438 cases and $41 million in losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In late October, Police named 27 Singaporeans and seven Malaysians suspected of running a Cambodian-based syndicate scam ring targeting Singapore believed to be behind at least 438 cases and $41 million in losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Police said that they are working with Interpol to issue red notices because these suspects are out of Singapore.

sections.label: Character and Citizenship Education classes
sections.summary: Character and Citizenship Education classes teach students to evaluate and verify online information sources and recognise and report online scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Today, our Character and Citizenship Education classes teach students to evaluate and verify credibility of online information sources to recognise and report different types of online scams, including phishing, online purchase scams and Internet love scams.

sections.label: Fighting scam stigma
sections.summary: The speaker mentions that part of scam resilience is fighting the stigma associated with falling prey to scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: On another note, I also just want to mention that part of scam resilience is also fighting the stigma associated with the person falling prey to scams.

sections.label: Report once pathway for victims
sections.summary: The public message is to report quickly, and a report once pathway would give victims a single case reference and spare them repeating details.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Our public message must be simple: report quickly, you are not alone, every minute counts.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Also, a "report once" pathway would give each victim a single case reference, would spare them from repeating the painful details from agencies to agencies or bank to bank.

sections.label: Laws, help and deterrence
sections.summary: The speaker says pairing strong laws with early help, empathy and survival voices reduces shame and improves recovery, and true deterrence needs a swift, certain, smart system.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In my view, if we pair strong laws and with early help, empathy at the front line and survival voices that breaks the stigma, we reduce shame, shorten response time and improve recovery.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But deterrence or true deterrence does not just come from harsher punishment alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It comes from a system that is swift, certain and smart.

sections.label: Scam losses statistics
sections.summary: In the first half of 2025 victims lost $456 million with almost 20,000 cases reported, and Police statistics show $1.1 billion lost in 2024 and over $651 million in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In the first half of 2025, victims lost $456 million, with almost 20,000 cases reported.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to statistics by the Police, scam victims lost $1.1 billion in 2024 and more than $651 million in 2023.

sections.label: Concert ticket reseller scams
sections.summary: Between 2023 and 2024, 1,500 people lost about $1.1 million in scams from online third-party resellers of concert tickets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Between 2023 and 2024, 1,500 people lost about $1.1 million in scams due to the sale of concert tickets by online third-party resellers.

sections.label: Overseas anti-ticketing scam laws
sections.summary: Japan and Taiwan have rolled out anti-ticketing scam laws, which the speaker hopes the Government would consider adopting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Some overseas jurisdictions with thriving entertainment industries, such as in Japan and in Taiwan, have already rolled out anti-ticketing scam laws to tackle this issue, something which I hope the Government would also consider adopting.

sections.label: SPF mid-year scam figures
sections.summary: SPF's Mid-Year Scam and Cybercrime Brief 2025 reported 22,476 scam and cybercrime cases from January to June and about $456 million lost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: According to the SPF's Mid-Year Scam and Cybercrime Brief 2025, there were 22,476 scam and cybercrime cases from January to June this year and the amount lost to scams was about $456 million.

sections.label: Caning for scammers and mules
sections.summary: Scammers, syndicate members and recruiters face mandatory caning of at least six strokes, while some scam mules face discretionary caning of up to 12 strokes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Scammers, members and recruiters of scam syndicates will face mandatory caning of at least six strokes, while scam mules who enable scammers in certain ways will face discretionary caning of up to 12 strokes.

sections.label: Caning for knowing scam mules
sections.summary: The article reports a surge in such scam cases in September and October, and the speaker asks why caning is not mandatory for scam mules who know they enable scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The same article also reports a "surge in such scam cases" in the months of September and October.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, in light of what I have shared, my question is: why is caning not made mandatory for scam mules as well, in particular, the mules who know that they are enabling or likely to enable scrams?

sections.label: Government official impersonation scams
sections.summary: SPF reported government officials impersonation scams almost tripled in the first six months of 2025, and on 26 October 2025 Police arrested 24 persons and investigated nine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: SPF's Mid-Year Scam and Cybercrime Brief 2025 also reported that "Government officials impersonation scams have almost tripled" in the first six months of 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And recently, on 26 October 2025, the Police shared that they had arrested 24 persons, investigating another nine for their suspected involvement in a case of government officials' impersonation scam.

sections.label: Caning penalties for scam offences
sections.summary: A Member asks if the Ministry would impose more severe penalties, such as doubling mandatory strokes, for scam offences involving Government impersonation, arguing for both enforcement and caning deterrents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In this vein, would the Ministry consider imposing even more severe penalties for scam-related offences, when there is an element of Government impersonation, such as by doubling the mandatory number of strokes, for example?

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Instead, he suggested that we strengthen enforcement bite to be more effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I would argue that we need both effective enforcement and deterrent in the form of caning to deal with the scourge of scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I will go further to say that we are able to remove mandatory caning for vandalism today and discussing it in this Bill because we have successfully deterred the act of vandalism from taking root in society in Singapore where there was a very threat several decades ago.

sections.label: Scam losses and deterrent message
sections.summary: The passage states the message that scamming Singaporeans carries a price, citing over $3.4 billion in losses since 2019 and a record $1.1 billion in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The message is clear, "If you dare to scam Singaporeans, this is the price you pay." This move is crucial due to devastating losses: over $3.4 billion since 2019, with a record $1.1 billion in 2024.

sections.label: Interim measures and fatal abuse penalties
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister to clarify interim measures and bank collaborations for Singaporeans in scam investigations who might not be convicted, and notes the Bill raises maximum jail for fatal abuse of vulnerable victims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can the Minister, therefore, clarify interim measures and collaborations with banks to support the increasing number of Singaporeans implicated in scam-related investigations but might not be convicted?

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes increasing maximum jail term for fatal abuse of vulnerable victims from 20 years to life imprisonment of up to 30 years.

sections.label: Migrant domestic worker abuse reports
sections.summary: Migrant domestic worker abuse averaged 320 reports annually from 2020 to 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, migrant domestic worker abuse averaged 320 reports annually from 2020 to 2024.

sections.label: Targeting scam syndicate kingpins
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister what steps are being taken to target the leaders of scam syndicates, the kingpins.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, can I ask the Minister, what steps are we taking to target the leaders of scam syndicates, in other words, the kingpin?

sections.label: Singaporeans leading scam networks
sections.summary: The passage notes worry that Singaporeans are involved in leading scam networks, citing three Singaporeans and 17 Singapore-registered entities recently sanctioned by the US over alleged transnational crypto scam activities linked to a Cambodian conglomerate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While we fight to support Singaporeans from scams, it is worrying to hear that there are Singaporeans being involved in leading scam networks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, three Singaporeans and 17 Singapore-registered entities were recently sanctioned by the US for alleged involvement in transnational crypto scam activities linked to a Cambodian conglomerate.

sections.label: Reviewing maximum caning age
sections.summary: It asks whether the maximum age for caning should be raised to 60 given lengthening health-spans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If age was intended to be a proxy of physical suitability, we should review if it is appropriate to increase the maximum age to 60, in view of our lengthening health-spans.

sections.label: Caning age limit and Bill support
sections.summary: It notes the caning age limit is 50, suggests raising it to 60, and expresses full support for the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Currently, the age limit for caning is at 50 years old.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, with longer healthy lifespan and society ageing, should we consider reviewing and raising this limit to 60 years old?

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I believe this would better reflect the current situation in our society and would be more effective as a deterrent. : Mr Speaker, notwithstanding these points for clarification and consideration, I express my full support for this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These amendments are timely, not just in offering tangible protection to Singaporeans, but also in inspiring public confidence that our criminal justice system is sensitive to emerging needs, especially in the realm of scams, it sends a clear signal that new ways to commit old crimes will be met with new penalties.

sections.label: Coverage of political officeholders and MPs
sections.summary: Political officeholders are covered as part of the executive, while MPs are not covered but MHA is reviewing this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Political officeholders are covered as they are part of the executive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: MPs are currently not covered but MHA is separately reviewing this.

sections.label: Scams via online platforms
sections.summary: In the first half of 2025, scammers approached victims online in about 82% of scam cases, with a Meta directive cited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In the first half of 2025, scammers used online platforms to approach victims in about 82% of all scam cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: For example, in September 2025, the Online Criminal Harms Act Competent Authority issued an implementation directive to Meta to put in place measures to target scam advertisements, accounts, profiles and/or business pages impersonating Government Office Holders on Facebook.

sections.label: FRONTIER+ intelligence sharing initiative
sections.summary: In October 2024 the Police formalised FRONTIER+ to strengthen real-time intelligence sharing, asset recovery and joint operations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: To cite one example, in October 2024, the Police formalised FRONTIER+, an initiative to strengthen real-time intelligence sharing, improve asset recovery and coordinate joint operations among the anti-scam units of several jurisdictions.

sections.label: Anti-scam operation arrests and recovery
sections.summary: Between May and June, an SPF-led FRONTIER+ operation with six jurisdictions led to 1,800 arrests and over $26 million recovered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Between May and June this year, SPF conducted one of the biggest anti-scam operations with six other jurisdictions under FRONTIER+, which led to the arrest of 1,800 persons and the recovery of more than $26 million.

sections.label: Scams and Cybercrime Brief 2025
sections.summary: The Police reported over 3,500 suspected money mules and scammers investigated in the first half of 2025, with over 500 charged.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: For example, in the Scams and Cybercrime Brief for the first half of 2025, the Police reported that more than 3,500 suspected money mules and scammers were investigated, of whom more than 500 were charged.

sections.label: I can ACT against scams survey
sections.summary: A survey found 89% of respondents found the campaign messages easy to understand and 84% were motivated to adopt anti-scam measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: A recent survey to measure the effectiveness of Singapore's "I can ACT against scams" campaign found that 89% of the respondents felt that the campaign messages were easy to understand, while 84% said that the campaign motivated them to adopt anti-scam protective measures.

sections.label: Discretionary caning for scam mules
sections.summary: Because scam mules have a range of culpability, caning is proposed to be discretionary so Courts decide if the facts warrant it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In reality, scam mules have a range of culpability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Therefore, we have proposed for caning to be discretionary to allow the Courts to decide if the facts of the case warrant the application of caning.

sections.label: Sentencing Advisory Panel scam guidelines
sections.summary: In August 2024 the inter-agency Sentencing Advisory Panel chaired by Justice Tay Yong Kwang issued sentencing guidelines for scams-related offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In August 2024, the inter-agency Sentencing Advisory Panel, chaired by Justice Tay Yong Kwang, issued sentencing guidelines for scams-related offences.

sections.label: Penalties apply after commencement
sections.summary: Only those who commit offences after the enhanced criminal penalties come into force can be liable for them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In other words, only those who commit offences after the enhanced criminal penalties come into force can be liable for them.

sections.label: MHA studying tighter scam penalties
sections.summary: MHA examined deterrence of new money laundering, Singpass and SIM card offences, and is studying proposals including returning seized scam assets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Specific to scams, MHA needed time to examine the deterrence effect of the new money laundering and Singpass offences that were operationalised in February 2024 and the new SIM card offences that were operationalised in January this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We think there is strong public interest to tighten the penalties further now, and caning would be commensurate with the severity of the scam problem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: As we stated in Parliament on 28 February 2025, we are studying various proposals, including the return of seized scam assets.

sections.label: Extradition Act question and scam syndicates
sections.summary: The speaker invites Ms Sylvia Lim to file a separate Parliamentary Question on the Extradition Act, noting SPF collaboration dismantled eight scam syndicates in the first half of 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: I invite Ms Sylvia Lim to file a separate Parliamentary Question on the usage of the Extradition Act as it goes beyond the scope of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: But I would like to highlight that SPF regularly collaborates with their foreign counterparts to enforce against transnational criminal syndicates and in the first half of 2025, eight scam syndicates were dismantled through such joint collaboration.

sections.label: Imprisonment in lieu of caning
sections.summary: An additional imprisonment term of up to 12 months can be imposed in lieu of caning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Second, an additional imprisonment term of up to 12 months can be imposed in lieu of caning.

sections.label: Children and Young Persons Act transmission
sections.summary: The amended Children and Young Persons Act provides that cases involving offenders aged 16 to below 18 may be transmitted to the State Court or High Court if they committed serious or repeat offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The amended Children and Young Persons Act only provides that cases involving offenders aged 16 to below 18 may be transmitted to the State Court or High Court if they have committed serious or repeat offences.

sections.label: Operation FRONTIER+ jurisdictions question
sections.summary: The question notes that Operation FRONTIER+ is a cross-border collaboration for joint intel sharing and joint ops, and that 13 jurisdictions are under the platform.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Earlier she mentioned Operation FRONTIER+, which is supposed to be a cross-border collaboration across jurisdictions for joint intel sharing as well as joint ops.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: My question is that she mentioned there are 13 jurisdictions under the platform.

sections.label: Cambodia not part of FRONTIER+
sections.summary: Cambodia is not part of FRONTIER+, but there are plurilateral and bilateral means of engaging counterparts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: At the moment, Cambodia is not part of FRONTIER+.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: However, we have both plurilateral as well as bilateral means of engaging our counterparts.
